text.title: Context Graph Failure Modes
text.summary: Six ways context graphs fail in production, each with the observable symptom and the rule that prevents it.

failure.symptom: Retrieval quality is flat or worse than the search it replaced, while cost rose an order of magnitude. Fact-shaped questions regressed most.
failure.cause: The data was hierarchical. Every real query resolved to a containment walk that a tree already answered.
failure.prevention: Name the warrant before building. Measured on GraphRAG-Bench: flat retrieval beat the graph on fact questions on both corpora at 1/40th the query tokens.

failure.symptom: Indexing dominates the budget; the graph is quietly not rebuilt after corpus changes; answers drift stale.
failure.cause: Edges were extracted by an LLM where they could have been derived from structure, so every rebuild repays full construction cost.
failure.prevention: Derive first. 654,673 tokens versus 89,215 on the same corpus is the difference between a graph you can rebuild nightly and one you rebuild once and then lie about.

failure.symptom: Intermittent failures on "connected" queries; latency spikes; truncation errors that never reproduce on test data.
failure.cause: No declared hop or fan-out bound, so traversal cost is O(k^h) and a well-connected seed node walks most of the graph.
failure.prevention: Declare h and k, compute the worst case, prove it fits before shipping.

failure.symptom: The agent asserts something that was true last quarter with no hedging, and cites the graph as its source.
failure.cause: Contradicting facts overwrote their predecessors, so the graph holds only a present tense with no way to express "no longer".
failure.prevention: Expire rather than delete; filter by validity at query time.

failure.symptom: The agent recommends a resource that does not exist, or reports "not found" for content that demonstrably does.
failure.cause: Edges point at identifiers that never resolved, or resolve on disk but not in the registry the retriever actually consults.
failure.prevention: Referential integrity as a failing CI gate, checked against the SAME registry the retriever uses at runtime — not against the filesystem. The two diverge silently, and the filesystem check passes while retrieval fails.

failure.symptom: A small number of queries are catastrophically slow or expensive; most are fine. The slow set all touch the same few nodes.
failure.cause: Hub nodes accumulated edges without bound, so any walk reaching them fans out to a large fraction of the graph.
failure.prevention: Declare a supernode cap and refactor hubs into intermediate nodes before shipping.
